acceptance_gates: PREDECLARE temporal split/run admission before candidate emission; no future rows or evaluator-only fixture data in predictor inputs
BASELINE gate: target-specific model must beat declared naive baseline on proper/point score; otherwise reject extra complexity
TIME_BASIS gate: every temporal predictor declares WALL_CLOCK/PULSE/EPISODE/CAUSAL_EVENT/FIXED_WINDOW semantics; no silent index-as-time
CALIBRATION gate: evaluate horizon-specific empirical coverage + width + proper score + reliability; aggregate coverage alone is insufficient
REGIME gate: include predeclared drift/regime-shift slices; static residual percentiles are not admitted as sufficient based on this experiment
OVERCONFIDENCE falsifier: same hard decisions with more extreme probabilities must be distinguishable by evaluator score
AUTHORITY gate: prediction/calibration/surprise never mints world truth, effect, completion, scheduler or canonical-state authority
COMPLEXITY gate: do not admit DLT/KTR/learned predictor until persistence/EWMA/seasonal/trend baselines establish target-level forecastability

external_research.f2_use: make horizon + distribution/interval explicit rather than a free-form confidence number
external_research.finding: point forecasts should be accompanied by uncertainty; multi-step uncertainty generally grows with horizon
external_research.source: Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3e — Distributional forecasts and prediction intervals

external_research.f2_use: proper scores belong in evaluator-side CalibrationReceipt, not in model authority
external_research.finding: quantile scores, Winkler interval score and CRPS evaluate probabilistic forecasts; lower is better
external_research.source: Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3e — Evaluating distributional forecast accuracy

external_research.f2_use: record both proper score and explicit reliability/ECE-style calibration evidence
external_research.finding: Brier/log loss are strictly proper but conflate calibration and discrimination; reliability/calibration curves are needed to inspect calibration itself

external_research.f2_use: calibration gate must test sequential/conditional coverage, not only aggregate coverage
external_research.finding: time dependence/distribution shift can violate nominal coverage; descriptive coverage/width alone can miss adaptation failures
external_research.source: Retzlaff et al. 2025, PMLR — Testing Marginal and Conditional Coverage in Conformal Prediction for Non-Stationary Time Series

external_research.f2_use: candidate next experiment: horizon-specific adaptive calibration; do not claim guarantees until exact assumptions/tests are satisfied
external_research.finding: adaptive conformal procedures can tune significance online and separately across horizons for non-exchangeable time series
external_research.source: Hallberg Szabadvary 2024, PMLR — Adaptive Coverage for Multi-Step Ahead Time-Series Forecasting Online

external_research.f2_use: treat adaptive calibration as a dedicated mechanism with explicit assumptions and falsifiers
external_research.finding: classical split-conformal exchangeability is violated by temporal dependence and shifts; recent methods reweight/update residual distributions or adapt target coverage
external_research.source: Stocker et al. 2025 review — Conformal Time Series Forecasting

external_research.f2_use: reuse temporal replay pattern, not Orbit truth/metric authority
external_research.finding: expanding and rolling temporal windows are native evaluation patterns
